name: Restructure the applicant table and CSV: applicant name first, resume in the table, job title and location dropped
request: Restructure the applicant table and CSV: applicant name first, resume in the table, job title and location dropped
checks: npm run check passed (typecheck, build, 364 tests, validate)
result: Restructured the applicant table and CSV around what they are read for. APPLICANT_TABLE_COLUMNS is now applicant_name, email, mobile, resume_file, resume_status, resume_link, current_role, current_company, total_experience, must_have_met, preferred_met, application_status, collected_at - the person first, then both ways to reach them, then the resume in three columns of its own. job_title and the applicant's location were dropped as columns as requested; both still show in the details drawer and job_id stays in the detail columns so the association survives. The detail columns gained all_emails and all_phone_numbers, which export every value rather than only the primary two, with each number marked as text per entry because a cell-level marker protects only the first line and 04423456789 would lose its leading zero. Also fixed a real defect found while restructuring: totalExperienceFrom handed calculateTotalExperience a {dates} object, which matches neither key it reads, so total_experience was always empty; it now passes {title, dateRange} and normalizeDateRange restores the separator in the applicant card's spaceless 2026-Present form, which parseDateRange deliberately refuses to split. The stored dateRange keeps LinkedIn's own wording and only a hyphen after a four-digit year is touched, so 3-5 years is still not a range. resume.pages added to the record and to the ApplicantRecord type.
